interface.title: Complexation Property Explorer
interface.field: Coordination chemistry / solution thermodynamics (metal–ligand stability constants)
interface.stage_of_work: Literature data lookup and curation before modelling or citing constants
interface.what_it_is_for: Search a read-only, merged SQLite database of metal–ligand stability constants (log K, ΔH, ΔS) by metal, ligand, ligand class, reaction type and measurement conditions; then inspect one record, compare it with another, check its literature references, and export the filtered set as CSV.

data.note: A seeded demo database, Complexation_Constants_Unified_rebuilt.db: 15 source records from 2 sources (NIST_SRD46 and LOCAL_SUPPLEMENT), 14 shown by default, 12 log K, 6 ligands, 3 linked references, and 1 strict cross-source duplicate (Ni-glycine: LOCAL_SUPPLEMENT·100002 = NIST·100013). It also holds the Fe-EDTA outlier (25.1), the non-numeric value 'ca. 9' (Ni-glycine 1:2), and a Zn-oxalate precipitation record with no temperature or ionic strength. I uploaded nothing.

screens_never_reached: Pages 2+ of the results (First/Prev/Next/Last and the Page box): the smallest page size is 25 and the demo has only 15 records, so the buttons stayed disabled
Records for ΔS and 'Other / unclassified' value types: listed in the dropdown, but I did not select them

The results table's built-in toolbar (Search, Show/hide columns, Download, Fullscreen): it appears in the page structure, but clicking its Search button timed out and the toolbar never showed in screenshots
not_done: Ni²⁺ by specific metal species was not resolved. The 'Metals and oxidation states' list shows Ni²⁺ twice, and choosing either one removed both from the list. Choosing the first Ni²⁺ gave 0 log K records (screens/018.webp, screens/019.webp). Choosing the second gave 1 result, the LOCAL_SUPPLEMENT duplicate, but at that point 'Only records with parsed numeric values' and 'Include 1 strict duplicate source records' were both ticked (screens/054.webp). The four NIST Ni records (100001, 100004, 100008, 100013) and the Ni-EDTA ΔH record appeared only with 'Search all metals' ticked (screens/019.webp, screens/021.webp, screens/023.webp, screens/024.webp, screens/054.webp). The reviewer read list_metals in database.py: it returns one entry per source metal species, ordered by metal_species_id, so the first Ni²⁺ is LOCAL_SUPPLEMENT:METAL:NI2, whose only record is the hidden duplicate. That explains the 0. Both attempts probably selected the LOCAL entry. This is most likely by-design per-source listing and not an app defect, but the NIST Ni²⁺ entry has not yet been tested on its own.

Row selection was unreliable: the first click on a row checkbox often did nothing and needed one or two more clicks (screens/007.webp). After the filters changed, the ticked row (NIST·100013) no longer matched the 'Selected record' line (LOCAL_SUPPLEMENT·100002) (screens/048.webp).

I did not select the Fe³⁺-citrate record named in the notes as the pair with no linked reference. I saw the same 'No linked references' state with Zn-citrate (which was selected automatically) and with Ni-glycine.
The 'Download as CSV' button in the table toolbar was not tried; the export was done with the app's own Prepare/Download CSV buttons.
I did not filter by the 1:4, protonation or precipitation reaction buckets, though those records were visible in the extended-column view (screens/048.webp).

No comparison was made between two records that differ in measurement conditions (temperature, ionic strength, electrolyte). The comparisons differed only by metal (Fe-EDTA vs Ni-EDTA) or only by Record ID (the duplicate pair).
